The 13 monthly changes from February 2025 through March 2026 average -0.376 million, but the FY2026 decline is much steeper: October-to-March participation fell 3.794 million. Level is therefore anchored at March's 37.298 million; momentum remains negative, while the shrinking March decline supplies a moderating adjustment."},{"kind":"text","text":"Mechanisms are separated as follows: level 37.298 million; momentum approximately -0.58 million per month over April-June; moderation adds about 0.10 million per month relative to the latest FY2026 trend; tighter eligibility and work rules retain a negative policy adjustment. These components imply about 35.55 million rather than simple flat persistence."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence-with-drift prior; historical sample is the 13 successive monthly changes from February 2025 through March 2026. Their sample standard deviation is sigma = 0.376 million, so the one-step 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 1.28*0.376 = 0.482 million. For a three-month horizon, scale by sqrt(3): 0.482*1.732 = 0.835, rounded to 0.84 million. Point = 37.298 - 1.748 = 35.550; bounds = 35.550 +/- 0.840 = [34.710, 36.390]."},{"kind":"text","text":"Upside risk: faster stabilization in enrollment or delayed implementation of tighter eligibility rules would land above 36.39 million. Downside risk: continued declines near the November-January pace, broad recertification losses, or unusually aggressive enforcement would land below 34.71 million, outside the interval."},{"kind":"forecast","point":35.55,"ciLow":34.71,"ciHigh":36.39}]}
